title: CCAR-F Mock Exam (60 questions)
credit: Source: 'Claude Certified Architect - Foundations Practice Question Set, Version 2' by Matthew Purcell (linkedin.com/in/purcellmatthew). Independent practice questions, not real exam content. Options and rationales have been condensed for the website. Get the author's permission before publishing this publicly.
notes: type 'single' = select ONE; 'multi' = select the number in 'pick'. answer is an array of letters. Domain ids: 1 Agentic, 2 Tool/MCP, 3 Claude Code, 4 Prompt/Structured Output, 5 Context/Reliability. Scenario ids match reference.json scenarios.

questions.q: You are implementing the support agent's core loop. Which control flow correctly decides when to keep executing tools and when to present the final response?

options.A: Loop until the assistant text contains a completion phrase like 'I have resolved the issue'
options.B: Inspect stop_reason: while 'tool_use' run the tools and return results; when 'end_turn' present the final response
options.C: Cap the loop at a fixed maximum iteration count and treat reaching the cap as completion
options.D: Stop whenever a response contains a text block, since the model only produces text once finished with tools

questions.why: stop_reason is the designed termination signal. A parses natural language (anti-pattern); C makes a cap the primary stop instead of a safety valve; D fails because responses can contain text and tool_use together.

questions.q: The agent calls lookup_order and your code executes it. How does the model actually receive the order data?

options.A: The MCP server streams the result straight into the model's active context
options.B: The result is attached to the tool's definition, which the model re-reads next pass
options.C: Nothing is required: the API executes tools and incorporates results automatically
options.D: Your code appends a tool result block referencing the tool call's ID and sends the updated message history in the next request

questions.why: Tool execution is the harness's job. The growing message history is the only channel through which the model sees tool results.

questions.q: Policy caps autonomous refunds at $500. In testing, prompt instructions alone still let a $650 refund through. What is the correct enforcement design?

options.A: A hook that intercepts outgoing process_refund calls, blocking amounts above $500 and redirecting to escalate_to_human
options.B: Move the limit to the top of the system prompt, restate it every turn, bold the amount
options.C: Lower sampling temperature to zero
options.D: Add the limit to the process_refund tool description and input schema

questions.why: Financial rules need deterministic enforcement. B and D only improve the odds; C makes sampling deterministic, not the policy binding.

questions.q: A customer writes one message with three concerns: a refund for a damaged item, a shipping address change, and a missing loyalty credit. How should the agent handle it?

options.A: Resolve the refund first, then ask whether they want help with the rest
options.B: Escalate to a human, since multi-issue sessions risk partially completed work
options.C: Decompose into three distinct items, investigate each against shared customer context, then respond with one unified resolution
options.D: Ask which issue matters most and resolve only that one

questions.why: Multi-concern decomposition with one unified answer protects first-contact resolution. A and D defer stated concerns; B escalates work within capability.

questions.q: The agent must escalate a complex billing dispute. Human agents do not have access to the conversation transcript. What should the escalation include?

options.A: Customer identity and issue category only, so the human forms an independent view
options.B: A structured handoff summary: customer ID, root cause analysis so far, relevant amounts and order numbers, and the recommended action
options.C: A sentiment summary and urgency rating
options.D: The complete raw tool results from the session

questions.why: The receiver has no transcript, so the summary must carry case state. A discards the investigation; C conveys mood not state; D is unprocessed noise.

questions.q: When process_refund fails it returns 'Operation failed.' The agent retries policy-blocked refunds and gives up on temporary outages. What is the fix?

options.A: Add a system prompt rule to retry any failed call twice with backoff
options.B: Catch failures in the harness and retry there so the agent only sees successes
options.C: Log every failure with category and cause for later analytics
options.D: Return structured error metadata: errorCategory (transient/validation/business), isRetryable boolean, and a short description

questions.why: Structured metadata lets the agent retry transient errors, explain business refusals, and stop wasting attempts. A hard-codes one strategy; B hides refusals; C gives no signal at decision time.

questions.q: A refund request violates the returns window policy and the tool rejects it. Which error response lets the agent handle it correctly with the customer?

options.A: errorCategory 'business', retriable false, plus a customer-friendly explanation of the policy
options.B: errorCategory 'validation', prompting the agent to correct parameters and retry
options.C: A success result with an empty refund object
options.D: The policy engine's full rejection payload including internal rule identifiers

questions.why: Policy violations are non-retryable business errors with a relayable explanation. B invites futile retries; C is silent suppression; D exposes internals.

questions.q: The agent often confuses get_customer and lookup_order; both have one-line descriptions. Which TWO changes most directly fix the misrouting?

options.A: Merge them into a single customer_lookup tool with a mode parameter
options.B: Document each tool's expected input formats and add example queries it should handle
options.C: Move selection guidance into the system prompt and keep descriptions minimal
options.D: Add boundary language, e.g. 'use lookup_order when an order number is present; use get_customer to verify identity'
options.E: Reorder the tool list so the most used tool is first

questions.why: Descriptions are the primary selection mechanism. A hides the problem in a mode parameter; C moves the signal away from where selection happens; E relies on unreliable ordering effects.

questions.q: A customer's first message: 'I want to speak to a human. Do not try to fix this yourself.' The issue looks like a routine replacement. What should the agent do?

options.A: Attempt resolution first, escalate only if it fails
options.B: Run sentiment analysis and escalate only if frustration exceeds a threshold
options.C: Escalate immediately, honoring the explicit request without first investigating
options.D: Acknowledge, but first gather order details so the human gets a complete handoff

questions.why: An explicit request for a human is a first-class escalation trigger. A and D keep working a case the customer closed; B uses an unreliable proxy.

questions.q: In long multi-issue sessions the agent misquotes refund amounts and order numbers because earlier details were condensed into vague summaries, while each lookup_order result dumps 40+ fields into context. Which TWO changes address this?

options.A: Extract transactional facts (amounts, dates, order numbers) into a persistent case-facts block outside the summarized history
options.B: Increase max_tokens on each request
options.C: Summarize after every turn instead of at the context threshold
options.D: Trim each tool result to only the fields relevant to the current issue before it enters context
options.E: Instruct the model to quote amounts only from the most recent summary

questions.why: Persist exact facts outside lossy summaries and trim bloat at the source. B, C and E intensify or ignore the lossy-summary problem.

questions.q: You have a personal /scratch-notes slash command that should not appear for teammates who pull the repo. Where does the file belong?

options.A: .claude/commands/ in the repo with a naming prefix
options.B: The root CLAUDE.md under a # Commands heading
options.C: ~/.claude/commands/ in your home directory
options.D: .claude/rules/ with a paths glob matching your username

questions.why: ~/.claude/commands/ is personal; .claude/commands/ ships to every clone. B is context not commands; D misuses path-scoped rules.

questions.q: Your /analyze-architecture skill produces thousands of lines of exploration output that pollute the main conversation. Which SKILL.md frontmatter option fixes this?

options.A: argument-hint
options.B: context: fork, running the skill in an isolated sub-agent and returning only its result
options.C: allowed-tools restricting to read-only
options.D: paths

questions.why: context: fork isolates verbose output. A and D narrow what is examined; C restricts tools, not where output accumulates.

questions.q: A /scaffold-component skill must be able to create files but never run shell commands, whatever its instructions say. How do you enforce this?

options.A: State 'never run Bash' prominently in SKILL.md
options.B: A pre-execution hook that scans rendered instructions for shell commands
options.C: Run the skill only in plan mode
options.D: Set allowed-tools in SKILL.md frontmatter to the file-write tools needed, omitting Bash

questions.why: allowed-tools is a configuration guarantee. A is prompt-level; B inspects instructions not runtime invocations; C is not a per-skill restriction.

questions.q: A new teammate's Claude Code sessions ignore team coding standards, which live in your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. What is the fix and how do you verify?

options.A: Move the standards into the project-level CLAUDE.md in the repo and use /memory to verify what a session loaded
options.B: Have the teammate copy your ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md into their home directory
options.C: Add the standards to .claude/settings.json
options.D: Publish the standards as a /standards slash command

questions.why: User-level config never travels via version control. B drifts; C misuses settings.json (permissions/tool settings); D makes standards opt-in.

questions.q: The project's CLAUDE.md has grown to 2,000 lines covering testing, API conventions, deployment and styling, all loaded regardless of task. What is the recommended reorganization?

options.A: Trim to a concise 200-line summary and rely on the model to infer details
options.B: Move everything to each developer's user-level CLAUDE.md
options.C: Split into topic-specific files in .claude/rules/ (testing.md, api-conventions.md, deployment.md), path-scoped where relevant
options.D: Convert it into slash commands developers run manually

questions.why: Rules files are the modular alternative with optional path scoping. A loses specifics; B unshares config; D makes always-relevant standards forgettable.

questions.q: Yesterday you ran a long investigation in a session named leak-hunt. Today you want to continue exactly where it left off. What do you run?

options.A: claude --continue
options.B: claude --resume leak-hunt
options.C: claude -p 'continue the leak investigation'
options.D: A new session relying on CLAUDE.md to restore the investigation context

questions.why: Named session resumption restores that conversation's context. A reopens whichever session is most recent; C starts a fresh run; D restores conventions, not discoveries.

questions.q: After a thorough module analysis you want to compare two refactoring strategies independently from the same baseline without cross-contamination. Which capability fits?

options.A: Run both sequentially in one session, asking Claude to forget the first
options.B: Open two new sessions and paste the conclusions into each
options.C: Use /compact between strategies
options.D: Use fork_session to create two independent branches from the shared baseline

questions.why: fork_session carries the full analysis into both branches. A is impossible; B is a lossy manual summary; C compresses but does not branch.

questions.q: You want to resume last week's refactoring session, but the team has merged substantial changes across the analyzed files, so most tool results describe code that no longer exists. What is the reliable approach?

options.A: Start a new session seeded with a structured summary of prior conclusions
options.B: Resume as-is; Claude automatically detects file changes
options.C: Resume and run /compact first
options.D: Resume and ask Claude to re-read each changed file incrementally

questions.why: Stale tool results make resumption unreliable. B assumes automatic re-verification; C compacts falsehoods; D leaves contradictory old and new states in one context.

questions.q: Mid-way through an extended exploration session, context is filling with verbose discovery output and responses are degrading, but you are not ready to end the session. Which built-in command helps immediately?

options.A: /memory
options.B: /rewind
options.C: /compact
options.D: /rules

questions.why: /compact compresses the conversation so the session can continue. B discards discoveries along with noise; A and D do not address conversation bloat.

questions.q: During multi-hour exploration the agent starts answering from 'typical patterns' instead of specific classes it found earlier. Which TWO practices counteract this context degradation?

options.A: Switch to a model with a larger context window and keep accumulating
options.B: Maintain a scratchpad file of key findings and have the agent reference it
options.C: Periodically paste the full list of discovered classes back into the conversation
options.D: Add a system prompt instruction to always answer from discovered code
options.E: Delegate verbose investigation to subagents that return summaries, keeping the main session for coordination

questions.why: Both manage what occupies context. A postpones the problem; C re-adds bulk to saturated context; D instructs without restoring the degraded signal.

questions.q: The coordinator's prompt says to delegate research to subagents but at runtime it never spawns any. Its configuration restricts it to research-planning tools. Most likely cause?

options.A: Its model tier lacks the reasoning depth for delegation
options.B: Subagent AgentDefinition descriptions are too vague
options.C: The prompt describes delegation generally but never names specific subagents
options.D: The coordinator's allowedTools does not include 'Task'

questions.why: Subagents are spawned through the Task tool. Without it, delegation is impossible no matter how good the prompt is.

questions.q: The web search subagent gathers excellent findings, but the synthesis subagent's reports are generic and cite none of them. The coordinator invokes synthesis with 'Synthesize the research findings.' What is wrong?

options.A: The synthesis model needs extended thinking
options.B: Subagents do not inherit the coordinator's history; findings must be passed explicitly in the synthesis prompt
options.C: The synthesis agent needs web search tools
options.D: The synthesis output schema is too loose

questions.why: Subagent context is isolated: each sees only what its prompt contains. The other options add capability over an empty input.

questions.q: The coordinator invokes the web search subagent, waits, then invokes the document analysis subagent, doubling latency though the tasks are independent. How do you run them in parallel?

options.A: Have the coordinator emit both Task tool calls in a single response
options.B: Enable streaming on both invocations
options.C: Move both to a faster model tier
options.D: Have the search subagent spawn the document analysis subagent when done

questions.why: Parallel spawning = multiple Task calls in one response. B changes delivery; C shortens tasks but still runs them end to end; D re-creates the sequential dependency.

questions.q: The coordinator gives subagents rigid step-by-step procedures ('run these exact five queries in this order') and they fail whenever a topic doesn't fit. How should coordinator prompts be designed?

options.A: Make procedures longer, covering more contingencies
options.B: Give the research goal only, omitting quality criteria
options.C: Specify research goals and quality criteria (what a complete answer looks like) and let the subagent adapt its approach
options.D: Route off-script topics back to the coordinator for a revised procedure

questions.why: Goal-and-criteria prompts preserve subagent adaptability. A is an arms race; B removes the definition of success; D adds round trips.

questions.q: Completed reports are coherent but shallow on some subtopics. You want the system to notice and repair its own coverage gaps before finalizing. Which pattern?

options.A: A final review subagent that scores quality and appends its assessment
options.B: An iterative loop: evaluate synthesis for gaps, re-delegate targeted research, re-synthesize until coverage is sufficient
options.C: Ask the report agent to pad thin sections with general knowledge
options.D: Always run every subagent exactly twice

questions.why: Iterative refinement closes the loop. A detects but ships the defect; C adds uncited generalities; D doubles cost blindly.

questions.q: Every subagent receives the full 18-tool catalog. The synthesis agent attempts web searches and the search agent tries document parsing, with frequent wrong-tool selections. What is the correct redesign?

options.A: Add a routing tool the agents call first
options.B: Group the catalog by category with headers
options.C: Write longer system prompts warning each agent which tools to ignore
options.D: Scope each subagent's tool set to its role, a handful of relevant tools each

questions.why: Agents choose more reliably among 4-5 role-relevant tools than 18. A adds a selection step; B reorganizes the same inventory; C fights an inventory problem with prompts.

questions.q: Subagents burn many tool calls just discovering what data exists (listing collections, probing issue summaries, checking schemas) before real work begins. Which MCP capability reduces this?

options.A: Expose content catalogs (document hierarchies, issue summaries, schema listings) as MCP resources
options.B: Increase the tool-call budget
options.C: Hard-code the data inventory into every system prompt
options.D: Add a describe_available_data tool every agent calls at startup

questions.why: Resources are the protocol's primitive for exposing content catalogs. B pays for the inefficiency; C goes stale; D rebuilds it as a bespoke tool.

questions.q: Final reports state findings but cite nothing; each summarization step compresses attribution away. What is the structural fix?

options.A: Have the report generator add plausible citations at the end
options.B: Instruct each summarizer to append a bibliography of consulted sources
options.C: Require subagents to output structured claim-source mappings that every downstream agent preserves through synthesis
options.D: Reduce summarization to one step

questions.why: Provenance survives only if structural. A invents citations; B lists sources without binding them to claims; D still strips attribution once.

questions.q: Two credible sources report different figures for the same market's size, and one subagent's summary simply picked the larger number. Which TWO practices handle conflicting data correctly?

options.A: Annotate the conflict explicitly (both values with sources) and let the coordinator reconcile before synthesis
options.B: Average the two figures
options.C: Always adopt the more recent source and discard the other
options.D: Require publication or data-collection dates in subagents' structured outputs
options.E: Have the subagent rank sources by credibility and report only the higher-ranked figure

questions.why: Conflicts are information: keep both with attribution and carry dates, since figures often measure different moments. B invents a number; C and E silently pick one.

questions.q: You are designing how the web search subagent behaves when searches fail or return nothing. Which TWO behaviors are correct?

options.A: On any failure, halt the workflow and surface the error to the operator
options.B: Attempt local recovery for transient failures and propagate unresolvable errors to the coordinator with any partial results
options.C: Return empty results marked as success when a search fails
options.D: Standardize all failures to a single 'search unavailable' status
options.E: Distinguish access failures (timeouts, service errors) from valid empty results

questions.why: Layered, honest propagation. A makes any failure fatal; C is silent suppression; D discards recovery context.

questions.q: The agent must (a) locate every file matching the test naming convention anywhere in the repo and (b) find every place the string 'PaymentDeclinedError' appears in code. Which TWO tool selections are correct?

options.A: Glob with a pattern like **/*.test.tsx for the test files
options.B: Grep with a filename pattern to find the test files
options.C: Grep for 'PaymentDeclinedError' in file contents
options.D: Glob for 'PaymentDeclinedError' across file contents
options.E: Bash running grep -r for both tasks

questions.why: Glob matches paths; Grep searches contents. B and D swap them; E bypasses the purpose-built tools.

questions.q: The agent attempts an Edit on a legacy file and fails: the anchor text appears in six places so the unique-match requirement cannot be satisfied. What is the standard fallback?

options.A: Delete five of the six occurrences
options.B: Run Edit with a replace-all option
options.C: Switch to Bash and modify the file with sed
options.D: Use Read to load the full file, then Write the complete modified content

questions.why: Read + Write is the documented fallback when Edit's unique match fails.

questions.q: Asked how the billing module works, the agent Reads dozens of files upfront and exhausts its context before answering. What is the correct exploration strategy?

options.A: Read files in alphabetical order and stop at the context limit
options.B: Work incrementally: Grep to find entry points, then Read selectively to trace flows from those anchors
options.C: Read the entry-point file in full and answer from it
options.D: Read only the README and docstrings

questions.why: Search first, then read narrowly along traced paths.

questions.q: The team shares a GitHub MCP server needing an auth token, and you also run a personal experimental MCP server. How should these be configured?

options.A: Shared server in project-scoped .mcp.json with env-var expansion (${GITHUB_TOKEN}); personal one in ~/.claude.json
options.B: Both in .mcp.json with the token pasted in
options.C: Both in ~/.claude.json with setup documented in the team wiki
options.D: Shared server in CLAUDE.md and personal in .claude/commands/

questions.why: Scoping follows audience. B commits a secret; C makes shared infra a manual chore; D uses files that do not configure servers.

questions.q: Two tasks: fixing an off-by-one bug in one function with a clear stack trace, and migrating the codebase's HTTP library across 45+ files with several viable approaches. How should plan mode and direct execution be assigned?

options.A: Plan mode for both
options.B: Direct execution for both
options.C: Direct execution for the well-scoped bug fix; plan mode for the 45-file migration
options.D: Plan mode for the bug fix and direct execution for the migration

questions.why: Direct for simple well-scoped changes; plan where scale and competing approaches make design-first valuable.

questions.q: Developers keep invoking your /generate-fixture skill bare, without the entity type and record count it needs. Which frontmatter option addresses this?

options.A: context: fork
options.B: allowed-tools
options.C: A more detailed description block documenting parameters
options.D: argument-hint, which prompts for the required parameters when invoked bare

questions.why: argument-hint is the mechanism for skills that need parameters. A isolates output; B constrains tools; C documents but the invocation still runs bare.

questions.q: Where should (1) the team's universal coding standards and (2) a multi-step release-notes workflow used a few times a month live?

options.A: Both as skills in .claude/skills/
options.B: Standards in CLAUDE.md (always loaded); release-notes workflow as a skill in .claude/skills/ (on demand)
options.C: Both in CLAUDE.md
options.D: Standards as a skill; release workflow in CLAUDE.md

questions.why: CLAUDE.md for universal always-relevant standards; skills for on-demand task workflows.

questions.q: The task is open-ended: 'add comprehensive tests to this legacy codebase.' Nobody knows where the risk concentrates. Which decomposition approach fits?

options.A: First map the codebase structure, identify high-impact areas, then create a prioritized plan that adapts as surprises emerge
options.B: Write tests file by file in directory order
options.C: Generate the full test suite in one request
options.D: Prioritize code with the most recent commits

questions.why: Open-ended tasks need adaptive decomposition. D uses recency as a proxy for importance; legacy risk often lives in old code.

questions.q: Choose decomposition strategies for two workflows: a code review that always checks the same five aspects, and a production-incident investigation whose next step depends on each finding. Which pairing is right?

options.A: Dynamic decomposition for both
options.B: Prompt chaining for both
options.C: Prompt chaining for the five-aspect review; dynamic adaptive decomposition for the investigation
options.D: Dynamic for the review; prompt chaining for the investigation

questions.why: Fixed pipelines for predictable work; adaptive decomposition where the path emerges from findings.

questions.q: You are writing AgentDefinition configurations for subagents. Which TWO statements are accurate?

options.A: Subagents automatically inherit the parent's full conversation history
options.B: Each subagent's AgentDefinition carries its own description, system prompt, and tool restrictions
options.C: Subagents can inherit the parent's context by setting an inherit flag
options.D: Subagents do not share memory between invocations; needed context must be provided explicitly in the prompt
options.E: Tool restrictions apply only to MCP tools, not built-ins like Bash or Write

questions.why: Subagents are individually configured and isolated. No inherited history, no inherit flag, and restrictions bind built-in and MCP tools alike.

questions.q: Your CI job must run Claude Code non-interactively and produce review findings the pipeline can parse and post as inline PR comments. Which invocation is correct?

options.A: claude 'review this PR' piped through grep
options.B: claude -p 'review this PR' with --output-format json and --json-schema
options.C: claude --headless 'review this PR' --format json
options.D: claude -p 'review this PR' alone, then regex-parse the prose

questions.why: -p for non-interactive, --output-format json for machine-readable, --json-schema to enforce structure. C invents flags; A hangs; D regex-parses prose.

questions.q: CI-generated tests ignore your fixture library, duplicate helper setup, and test trivialities. Developers reject most of them. What is the configuration-level fix?

options.A: Generate three times as many tests
options.B: Have developers rewrite them as a standing chore
options.C: Lower generation temperature
options.D: Document testing standards, what makes a test valuable, and available fixtures in CLAUDE.md

questions.why: CI gets project context from CLAUDE.md. The model can only follow conventions it has been shown.

questions.q: Reviews re-run after each new commit and the bot re-posts the same findings every time. How should re-reviews be designed?

options.A: Include the prior review's findings in context and instruct Claude to report only new or still-unaddressed issues
options.B: Review only the newest commit's diff in isolation
options.C: Limit reviews to one per PR
options.D: Deduplicate by hashing each finding's file path and line number

questions.why: Duplicate suppression is a context-design problem. B misses interaction issues; C leaves later pushes unreviewed; D breaks when line numbers shift.

questions.q: When the same Claude Code session that generated a change also reviews it, the review is conspicuously gentle. Why, and what is the design implication?

options.A: The model is being polite; instruct it to be harsher
options.B: Reviews should use a larger model tier
options.C: A session keeps the reasoning that produced the code, biasing it toward its own decisions; review independently
options.D: Run reviews at temperature zero

questions.why: Session context isolation matters. A misreads a context effect as personality; B changes capability not contamination; D confuses sampling variance with context bias.

questions.q: Your review prompt says 'be conservative and only report high-confidence findings,' yet false positives remain high. What does effective precision engineering look like?

options.A: Add 'be very, very conservative'
options.B: Report all findings sorted by stated confidence
options.C: Reduce the number of files reviewed per run
options.D: Swap confidence wording for explicit criteria: which issue types to report, which to skip, and the boundaries between

questions.why: Specific criteria give the model an operable decision rule. A has no operational content; B reorders noise; C reviews less with the same faulty judgment.

questions.q: 'Code style' findings are 70% false positives and developers have begun dismissing security findings too. What is the right operational move?

options.A: Ship more style findings to show the category's importance
options.B: Temporarily disable the style category to protect trust in accurate categories while its prompts are improved
options.C: Rename 'code style' to 'code quality'
options.D: Keep every category live with a banner asking for patience

questions.why: High-FP categories are contagious. Disable, fix offline, re-enable.

questions.q: The reviewer labels near-identical issues 'critical' one day and 'minor' the next, making severity-based merge gates unreliable. How do you get consistent severity?

options.A: Define explicit severity criteria with concrete code examples for each level
options.B: Remove severity levels
options.C: Sample severity three times and take the majority vote
options.D: Map severity to line count

questions.why: Operational definitions anchored by examples turn a vibe into a rubric. C reduces noise but leaves the judgment unanchored; D measures size not impact.

questions.q: The reviewer keeps flagging your codebase's accepted idiomatic patterns (e.g. intentional commented fall-throughs) as bugs, and detailed prose instructions haven't fixed it. What is the most effective addition?

options.A: A rule that anything containing a comment is acceptable
options.B: An instruction to defer to the codebase's existing conventions
options.C: Few-shot examples contrasting accepted patterns with genuine issues, showing why each is or isn't reportable
options.D: A ban on reviewing files with idiomatic patterns

questions.why: When prose fails to convey a judgment boundary, contrasted examples with reasoning carry it.

questions.q: Your team is deciding which CI workloads to move to the Message Batches API for its 50% cost savings. Which TWO statements are accurate?

options.A: Batch processing suits latency-tolerant, non-blocking workloads like nightly test generation and weekly audit reports
options.B: Batches are guaranteed to complete within one hour off-peak, making them viable for pre-merge checks
options.C: The batch API supports multi-turn tool calling within a single request
options.D: Blocking workflows such as pre-merge checks should stay on the synchronous API
options.E: Batch results are returned in submission order

questions.why: No completion-time guarantee, no mid-request tool execution, and results are correlated by custom_id, not position.

questions.q: You are adding few-shot examples to the review prompt. Which TWO practices reflect how few-shot prompting works best?

options.A: Include as many examples as possible (20+)
options.B: Use 2-4 targeted examples aimed at ambiguous scenarios, showing why one action beats plausible alternatives
options.C: Once examples are added, explicit criteria become unnecessary
options.D: Prefer abstract placeholder examples over real project code
options.E: Include examples demonstrating the exact desired output format (location, issue, severity, fix)

questions.why: Targeted and demonstrative beats volume. Examples complement explicit criteria, and realistic cases are what transfer.

questions.q: Your pipeline asks Claude to 'respond with JSON' in plain text; parsing breaks on markdown fences, trailing commentary and malformed syntax. What is the most reliable structural fix?

options.A: Strengthen the prompt: 'respond ONLY with valid JSON'
options.B: Post-process with regexes that strip fences and repair syntax
options.C: Define the extraction as a tool whose input schema is your JSON schema, and read the data from the tool_use block
options.D: Switch the output format to YAML

questions.why: Tool use with a JSON schema eliminates syntax errors by construction. A, B and D stay in a text-shaped channel.

questions.q: You have several extraction tools, one per document type, and incoming documents of unknown type. The model must always produce a structured extraction and never reply with conversational text. Which tool_choice is correct?

options.A: tool_choice: 'any'
options.B: tool_choice: 'auto'
options.C: tool_choice forced to one named extraction tool for every document
options.D: Omit tool_choice and use strongly worded prompt instructions

questions.why: 'any' compels a tool call while letting the model choose the schema. B and D allow text; C welds every document to one schema.

questions.q: Your invoice schema marks vendor_tax_id as required. On invoices that lack a tax ID, the model fabricates plausible values. What is the schema-level fix?

options.A: Add a prompt instruction: 'never fabricate tax IDs'
options.B: Post-validate against the official checksum and discard failures
options.C: Lower the temperature
options.D: Make the field optional/nullable so the model can return null when the value is absent

questions.why: Required fields on possibly-absent data force fabrication. Nullable gives an honest answer.

questions.q: Since adopting tool use, extractions are always syntactically valid, yet invoices arrive where line items don't sum to the stated total and values occasionally land in the wrong fields. What should you understand and do?

options.A: Schema compliance was falsely advertised; file a bug
options.B: Schemas ensure structure, not semantics; add validation: extract calculated_total vs stated_total and flag mismatches with a conflict_detected flag
options.C: Relax numeric fields to unconstrained strings
options.D: Re-run affected extractions with the discrepancy described in the retry prompt

questions.why: Tool use guarantees structure, not truth. D presupposes the discrepancy was already detected, which is the validation layer you are adding.

questions.q: An extraction fails Pydantic validation with two specific field errors. You will retry. What should the retry contain, and when would you skip retrying?

options.A: Validation errors plus a stricter instruction; skip after any second consecutive failure
options.B: The failed extraction plus the errors; retry up to a fixed attempt budget every time
options.C: The original document, the failed extraction, and the validation errors; skip retrying when the information is absent from the source
options.D: The original document with a fresh prompt and no reference to the failure; skip only on API errors

questions.why: The model needs the source, its prior output and the errors. Format errors are retryable; absent information is not.

questions.q: An overnight batch of 10,000 documents completes with 200 failures: mostly oversized documents that blew past context limits, plus some transient errors. What is the correct workflow?

options.A: Identify failed requests by custom_id and resubmit only those, chunking oversized documents first
options.B: Resubmit the entire batch and keep whichever results arrive first
options.C: Log the 200 failures for weekly manual review and accept the batch as complete
options.D: Switch the 200 to the synchronous API unchanged

questions.why: Fix each failure's cause and pay for 200, not 10,000. D misunderstands that context limits belong to the model, not the API path.

questions.q: A single analyze_document tool handles extraction, summarization and claim verification via a mode parameter. The agent regularly picks the wrong mode. What is the recommended redesign?

options.A: Add a fourth mode that auto-detects the right mode
options.B: Document each mode's selection criteria far more thoroughly in the single description
options.C: Reduce to two modes by merging extraction into summarization
options.D: Split into purpose-specific tools: extract_data_points, summarize_content, verify_claim_against_source

questions.why: Purpose-specific tools turn a hidden mode decision into a visible selection decision.

questions.q: When your MCP extraction tool hits a parsing failure it returns 'Error: could not parse document' as an ordinary successful text result, and the agent treats that sentence as document content. What is the correct MCP pattern?

options.A: Prefix error text with 'SYSTEM ERROR:'
options.B: Return the failure with the MCP isError flag set
options.C: Return a structured JSON body with an error field inside the result text
options.D: Throw an unhandled exception and let the connection drop

questions.why: isError is MCP's channel for tool failure. C still delivers the error as a successful result; D turns a recoverable error into a transport breakdown.

questions.q: Your extraction system reports 97% aggregate accuracy and leadership wants to cut human review of high-confidence extractions. Which TWO practices must precede that decision?

options.A: Segment accuracy by document type and field, verifying consistent performance across every segment
options.B: Accept the aggregate as sufficient since 97% exceeds human reviewer accuracy
options.C: Implement stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions for ongoing error-rate measurement
options.D: Sunset the accuracy dashboard once review is reduced
options.E: Review only extractions the model itself flags as uncertain

questions.why: Segmentation shows the average isn't hiding a failing segment; stratified sampling keeps measuring after humans step back.

questions.q: Reviewer capacity covers only a fraction of extractions, so review must be routed where errors are likeliest. Which TWO practices form a sound routing design?

options.A: Trust the model's raw self-reported confidence without validation
options.B: Have the model output field-level confidence scores, then calibrate review thresholds against a labeled validation set
options.C: Review a fixed random 5% of all extractions
options.D: Route to human review extractions with low calibrated confidence or ambiguous source documents
options.E: Prioritize the longest and most complex documents

questions.why: Calibrate, then route by risk. Random samples measure error rates but do not route reviewers; length is a loose proxy.
